newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia shares ease, nervous Westerners sell-trade.
newsitem.headline: Russia shares ease, nervous Westerners sell-trade.

text.p: Leading Russian shares eased on Monday in thin trade and operators said some Western players had sold, following nervousness in major world markets.

The Russian Trading System index of 23 leading shares closed down at 282.23 from 286.03 on Friday on a slight $16.9 million total market turnover. Healthy turnover is generally considered more than double that amount.

Wall Street shares were higher at midday but Russian traders say major markets will have to remain calm for at least a couple of weeks before the Russian market, where trading is drying up, comes alive again.
Oil company LUKoil, which announced an increase in 1996 dividends, fell to $13.20 from $13.42.
Electric company UES closed down at $0.1831 from $0.1849 and regional energy utility Mosenergo eased to $1.121 from $1.169.

"Russians are not selling because they think its the bottom, but it's practically impossible to resist the (sell) volumes from the West," said senior trader at Bank MFK-Moscow Partners Alexei Abdurakhimov.
Rinaco Plus dealer Andrei Kukk said the market could stay quiet "as long as it wants".
